question.text: Zirconium phosphate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>Zr</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>PO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>]</mo></math> dissociates into three zirconium cations of charge​ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and four phosphate anions of charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. If molar solubility of zirconium phosphate is denoted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and its solubility product by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi>sp</mi></msub></math> then which of the following relationship between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi>sp</mi></msub></math> is correct ​?

options.text: <math><mrow>  <mtext>S</mtext>  <mo>=</mo>      <mrow>      <mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=",">        <mrow>          <msub>                  <mtext>K</mtext>                <mtext>sp</mtext>          </msub>          <mo>/</mo>          <msup>                <mrow>                  <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=",">                    <mrow>                      <mn>6</mn>                      <mn>9</mn>                      <mn>1</mn>                      <mn>2</mn>                    </mrow>                  </mfenced>                </mrow>              <mrow>                <mn>1</mn>                <mo>/</mo>                <mn>7</mn>              </mrow>          </msup>        </mrow>      </mfenced>    </mrow>  </mrow></math>

solution.text:
In the saturated solution of

Zr 3 PO 4 4 + aq ⇌ 3 Zr 4 + 3 S molar + 4 PO 4 3 - 4 S molar

K sp = Zr 4 + 3 PO 4 3 - 4 = 3 S 3 4 S 4

= 2 7 × 2 5 6 × s 7 = 6 9 1 2   S 7

S = K sp 6 9 1 2 1 / 7
